text: Glorietur autem frater humilis in sublimitate sua,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:8 ends the sentence on the doubter, and *Glōriētur autem frāter humilis* opens a new step, the lowly brother and the rich (1:9–11) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Omne bonum donum, omneque perfectum munus superne est, descendens a Patre luminum, apud quem nulla est mutatio, aut ulla conversionis umbra.
note: *ā Patre lūminum* capital, God the Father (ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν φώτων, BSB the Father of the heavenly lights; decision 20), as your *Deus et Pater* (4) and *Deō et Patrī* (2); 1573 prints *à patre luminum* (canvas 917), as it lowers *patre* everywhere (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Si quis sibi videtur esse religiosus apud vos, neque tamen linguam suam frenat, sed animum suum fallit, hujus vana est religio.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:25 closes the hearer and the doer with *beātus erit*, and *Sī quis sibi vidētur esse religiōsus* opens the test of religion (1:26–27); the BSB's breaks at 1:5, 1:12, 1:16 and 1:22 left, each verse running on by *Quod sī*, a closing beatitude, or *autem* with the *sermōnem* of 1:21 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Religio pura et impolluta apud Deum et Patrem haec est: curam gerere pupillorum et viduarum in eorum calamitate, et intaminatum se custodire a mundo.
note: *apud Deum et Patrem* capital, God the Father (παρὰ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί; decision 20), as your *Deus et Pater* (4) and *Deō et Patrī* (2) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Et vos in eum, qui vestem gestat splendidam, intueamini, eique dicatis: “Tu sede hic pulchre”: pauperi autem dicatis: “Tu istic sta, aut hic sub meo subsellio sede”:
note: the two speeches after *eīque dīcātis* and *pauperī autem dīcātis* are direct (imperatives *sedē*, *stā*): each in “…”, as the BSB, *Tū* capital as 1573 (*dicatis : Tu tede hic pulchre : pauperi autem dicatis , Tu iſtic ſta*, canvas 917); the draft's semicolon after the first *dīcātis* made a colon, as the second; the colons after the closing marks kept, the sentence running on to the question of 2:4, as your 1 Cor 1:12 *“Ego Apollō”: nōnne* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: nonne discrimen apud vos fecistis, et male cogitantes judices fuistis?
note: *nōnne* lower case: the apodosis of the conditional begun at 2:2 (*Nam sī quis …*), after 2:3's colon, as 1573 (*nónne a diſcrimen*, canvas 917) and your 1 Cor 1:12 *“Ego Apollō”: nōnne carnālēs estis?* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Siquidem legi paretis regiae, quae sic litteris est prodita: \\qt “Alterum ut teipsum diligito,”\\qt* recte facitis.
note: Lev 19:18 after *quæ sīc litterīs est prōdita:* (κατὰ τὴν γραφήν) in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB, the words of your Gal 5:14 (*\\qt “Alterum ut teipsum dīligitō.”\\qt**); *Alterum* capital as 1573 (*prodita , Alterum vt teipſum diligito : rectè facitis*, canvas 917) and Gal 5:14; the comma inside the marks, the sentence running on to *rēctē facitis*, as your Rom 13:9 *concupīscitō,”\\qt* et* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Nam qui dixit: \\qt “Ne adulterato,”\\qt* idem dixit: \\qt “Ne occidito.”\\qt* Quod si non adulteras, sed occidis, contra legem committis.
note: the two commandments (Exod 20:13–14) after *quī dīxit:* and *īdem dīxit:* in \\qt with “…”, as the BSB and as your Rom 13:9 (*\\qt “Nē adulterātō, nē occīditō …”\\qt**), *Nē* capital each time as 1573 (*Nam qui dixit , Ne adulterato : idem dixit , Ne occi dito*, canvas 917); the colon after *adulterātō* made a comma inside the marks, the sentence running on to *īdem dīxit* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Itaque dicet aliquis: “Tu fidem habes; ego opera habeo.” Ostende mihi tuam fidem sine tuis operibus; ego tibi ex meis operibus fidem meam ostendam.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 2:17 concludes (*Ita fidēs … mortua sit*), and *Itaque dīcet aliquis* opens the objector's challenge (2:18–19); the objector's words after *dīcet aliquis:* are direct (*tū … habēs; ego … habeō*): in “…”, *Tū* capital as 1573 (*dicet aliquis : Tu fidem habes , ego opera ha beo : oſtende*, canvas 917); closed after *habeō* and James's reply set apart by a full stop for the draft's colon, *Ostende* capital, as the BSB and the NRSV; **uncertain**: the objector's words can be read as running to the end of the verse (the Greek has no marks, and 1573's colon allows either) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Atque ita comprobatum est scriptum illud, quod sic habet: \\qt “Credidit Abrahamus Deo, idque ei justitiae ductum est,”\\qt* et Dei amicus est appellatus.
note: Gen 15:6 after *scrīptum illud, quod sīc habet:* in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB, as your Rom 4:3 (*\\qt “Crēdidit autem Abrāhāmus Deō, id quod eī jūstitiæ ductum est.”\\qt**) and Gal 3:6; *Crēdidit* capital as 1573 (*ſic habet : Credidit Abrahamus Deo*, canvas 918); closed before *et Deī amīcus est appellātus*, which is not in Gen 15:6 (Isa 41:8 and 2 Chr 20:7 call him so), as the BSB (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Frenos quidem equorum oribus adhibemus, ut nobis pareant, eorumque totum corpus agimus.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 3:2 ends the general statement (*quī possit etiam tōtum frēnāre corpus*), and *Frēnōs quidem* opens the images of the tongue (bit, rudder, fire), where 1573 sets its margin heading *De lingua* (canvas 918); the BSB's breaks at 3:5, 3:7 and 3:9 left, each continuing the image or the argument (*Sīc et lingua*, *Omnis enim*, *Ea …*) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Ea Deum et Patrem collaudamus: eadem homines exsecramur, ad Dei similitudinem factos:
note: *Deum et Patrem* capital, God the Father (TR τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα, SBLGNT τὸν κύριον καὶ πατέρα; decision 20), as 1:27 and your *Deus et Pater* (4) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: O degeneres et viri et feminae: nescitis, mundi amicitiam Dei esse inimicitias? Qui vult amicus esse mundi, inimicus efficitur Dei.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 4:3 ends the diagnosis of the quarrels, and *Ō dēgenerēs* opens a new step in direct apostrophe, friendship with the world (4:4–6) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: An putatis, illud inaniter esse litteris proditum? Scilicet ad invidiam propensus est is, qui in vobis habitat, Spiritus?
note: *Spīritus* capital, the Spirit of God dwelling in believers (τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν, BSB the Spirit He caused to dwell in us; decision 20), as your Rom 8:9 and 8:11 *Spīritus … habitat in vōbīs*; Castellio's ironic *Scīlicet …?* (surely the Spirit is not prone to envy) points the same way; **uncertain**: 1573 prints *ſpiritus* (canvas 918), the KJV and some readers take it as the human spirit; the question is left unmarked, not a quotation (the BSB has no marks; no OT verse says it) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: At majus confert beneficium. Itaque \\q1 \\qt “Deus (inquit ille) et superbis adversatur,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et modestorum fautor est.”\\qt*
note: Prov 3:34 (LXX) after *Itaque … inquit ille* (διὸ λέγει) as poetry in \\qt, two lines after the BSB, mid-verse as your Gal 4:27; *(inquit ille)* inside the marks in parentheses, as your Eph 4:8 *(inquit ille)* and Rom 14:11 *(inquit Dominus)*, for 1573's commas (*Itaq ; Deus , inquit il le , & ſuperbis aduerſatur*, canvas 918); *Itaque* is James's, outside, as Eph 4:8; *Deus* the quotation's first word (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Nolite alius alii detrahere: qui fratri detrahit, fratremque suum damnat, legi detrahit, legemque damnat. Quod si legem damnas, non legis exsecutor es, sed condemnator.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 4:10 closes the call to humility (*et vōs ēvehet*), and *Nōlīte alius aliī dētrahere* opens a new charge, against judging one another (4:11–12) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Age jam, qui dicitis: “Hodie aut cras proficiscemur in illam urbem, et illic unum annum agemus, et mercabimur, et lucrabimur,”
note: the traders' words after *quī dīcitis:* are direct (*proficīscēmur … lucrābimur*, first person): in “…”, as the BSB; *Hodiē* capital as 1573 (*qui dicitis : Hodie aut cras*, canvas 918); closed at the end of the verse with a comma for the draft's colon, the sentence running on to 4:14 *cum nesciātis* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: quum nesciatis, quid sit cras futurum. Qualis enim est vita vestra? Vapor est, qui paullisper exstat, deinde evanescit.
note: *cum* lower case: the clause depends on *quī dīcitis* of 4:13 (οἵτινες οὐκ ἐπίστασθε), as 1573 prints it (*14 cùm neſciatis quid ſit cras futurum*, canvas 919) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Quum dicere debeatis: “Si volet Dominus, et si vivemus, hoc aut illud faciemus.”
note: the words they ought to say, after *Cum dīcere dēbeātis:*, are direct (*vīvēmus … faciēmus*): in “…”, as the BSB; *Sī* capital as 1573 (*Cùm dicere debeatis : Si volet Dominus*, canvas 919); the BSB's paragraph at 4:15 left, *Cum dīcere dēbeātis* continuing the thought of 4:13–14 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Aurum et argentum aeruginosum, eorumque aerugo contra vos testimonium dicet, vestrasque carnes ignis in morem consumet. Poenam vobis congessistis in ultimum tempus.
note: *cōnsūmet.* with a full stop and *Pœnam* capital: *Pœnam vōbīs congessistis* is a new sentence (ἐθησαυρίσατε ἐν ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις, its own clause in the BSB after its break, and the KJV, NRSV), not a further object of *cōnsūmet*; 1573 prints a comma and a capital inside Castellio's marks (*in morem conſumet , L. Pœnam G. vobis congeſsiſtis*, canvas 919), the marks dropped by stage 2, so the capital is 1573's and the stop is the sentence's (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: In primis autem, mei fratres, ne juratote neque caelum, neque terram, nec aliud ullum jusjurandum: sed esto ejusmodi sermo vester, ut “etiam” sit etiam, et “non” non, ne in simulationem cadatis.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 5:11 closes the example of Job, and *In prīmīs autem, meī frātrēs* opens a new charge, on oaths; *“etiam”* and *“nōn”* in “…” as words named (decision 39), as the BSB (your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no) and your 2 Cor 1:17–20; the second *etiam* and *nōn* unmarked, predicates (let your yes be a true yes), as the BSB; **uncertain**: your Matt 5:37 marks the whole saying, both words (*‘etiam, etiam’, ‘nōn, nōn.’*), where Castellio's syntax differs (no *sit*) (Claude, 2026-11-12)
